teachings.text: Mind comes before all things; mind is their chief, and they are made by mind. Speak or act with a corrupted mind, and suffering follows, as the wheel follows the ox that pulls the cart.
teachings.shortText: Mind comes before all things. Act with a corrupted mind, and suffering follows.

teachings.text: Mind comes before all things; mind is their chief, and they are made by mind. Speak or act with a pure mind, and happiness follows, like a shadow that never leaves.
teachings.shortText: Act with a pure mind, and happiness follows like a shadow that never leaves.

teachings.text: “They insulted me, they hurt me, they defeated me, they robbed me.” Those who hold on to such thoughts never quiet their hatred.
teachings.shortText: Hold on to thoughts of being wronged, and hatred never quiets.

teachings.text: Hatred is never ended by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred ended. This is an eternal law.
teachings.shortText: Hatred is never ended by hatred. By non-hatred alone it ends.

teachings.text: Many forget that we must all one day die. Those who truly understand this let their quarrels come to rest.
teachings.shortText: Remember we must all one day die, and quarrels come to rest.

teachings.text: Heedfulness is the path to the deathless; heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless are as if already dead.
teachings.shortText: Heedfulness is the path to the deathless.

teachings.text: Through effort, heedfulness, discipline and self-control, the wise make of themselves an island that no flood can overwhelm.
teachings.shortText: Through effort and self-control, become an island no flood can overwhelm.

teachings.text: The restless, wavering mind is hard to guard and hard to hold back. The wise straighten it, as a fletcher straightens an arrow.
teachings.shortText: The wise straighten the restless mind, as a fletcher straightens an arrow.

teachings.text: The mind is hard to restrain, swift, and lands wherever it wishes. It is good to tame it. A tamed mind brings happiness.
teachings.shortText: It is good to tame the mind. A tamed mind brings happiness.

teachings.text: Neither mother, nor father, nor any other relative can do you as much good as your own well-directed mind.
teachings.shortText: No one can do you as much good as your own well-directed mind.

teachings.text: Do not dwell on the faults of others, on what they have done or left undone. Look instead at what you yourself have done and left undone.
teachings.shortText: Look not at others' faults, but at what you have done and left undone.

teachings.text: Like a beautiful flower that is bright in color but has no scent are the fine words of one who does not live by them.
teachings.shortText: Fine words not lived by are like a bright flower with no scent.

teachings.text: “I have children, I have wealth” — so the fool worries. But one does not even own oneself. How then children? How then wealth?
teachings.shortText: We do not even own ourselves. How then can we own children or wealth?

teachings.text: A fool who knows their foolishness is, to that extent, wise. But a fool who thinks themselves wise is a fool indeed.
teachings.shortText: A fool who knows their foolishness is, to that extent, wise.

teachings.text: Should you find a wise person who points out your faults, follow them as you would a guide to hidden treasure.
teachings.shortText: One who points out your faults is a guide to hidden treasure.

teachings.text: Irrigators guide water, fletchers shape arrows, carpenters shape wood. The wise shape themselves.
teachings.shortText: Carpenters shape wood. The wise shape themselves.

teachings.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by praise or blame.
teachings.shortText: As a rock is unshaken by wind, the wise are unmoved by praise or blame.

teachings.text: Better than a thousand empty words is a single meaningful word that brings peace to the one who hears it.
teachings.shortText: Better than a thousand empty words is one word that brings peace.

teachings.text: One may conquer a thousand times a thousand people in battle, yet the one who conquers themselves is the greatest of victors.
teachings.shortText: The one who conquers themselves is the greatest of victors.

teachings.text: Hurry toward the good and hold your mind back from harm. When one is slow to do good, the mind begins to delight in harm.
teachings.shortText: Hurry toward the good, and hold your mind back from harm.

teachings.text: Do not think lightly of good, saying, “It will not come to me.” Drop by drop the water jar is filled; little by little, the wise fill themselves with good.
teachings.shortText: Drop by drop the jar is filled. Little by little, the wise fill with good.

teachings.text: All tremble at violence; all fear death. Seeing others as yourself, do not harm and do not cause harm.
teachings.shortText: All fear violence. Seeing others as yourself, do no harm.

teachings.text: Do not speak harshly to anyone. Those spoken to harshly will answer you in kind.
teachings.shortText: Speak harshly to no one; harsh words return to you in kind.

teachings.text: You are your own refuge; who else could be your refuge? With yourself well tamed, you find a refuge that is hard to find.
teachings.shortText: You are your own refuge. Who else could be?

teachings.text: By yourself is harm done, and by yourself you are stained. By yourself harm is left undone, and by yourself you are made pure. Purity and impurity depend on you; no one can purify another.
teachings.shortText: Purity depends on yourself. No one can purify another.

teachings.text: Hard it is to be born human, hard is the life of mortals, hard it is to hear the true teaching, and rare is the arising of a Buddha.
teachings.shortText: Hard it is to be born human. Rare it is to hear the true teaching.

teachings.text: To avoid all harm, to cultivate the good, and to purify one's own mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
teachings.shortText: Avoid harm, cultivate good, purify the mind.

teachings.text: How happily we live, free from hatred among those who hate. Among people who hate, we dwell without hatred.
teachings.shortText: How happily we live, free from hatred among those who hate.

teachings.text: Victory breeds hatred; the defeated live in pain. The peaceful live happily, having set aside both victory and defeat.
teachings.shortText: The peaceful live happily, setting aside both victory and defeat.

teachings.text: Health is the greatest gain, contentment the greatest wealth, trust the best of relatives, and Nibbāna the highest happiness.
teachings.shortText: Health is the greatest gain; contentment, the greatest wealth.

teachings.text: Overcome anger with calm, overcome harm with good, overcome stinginess with giving, overcome the liar with truth.
teachings.shortText: Overcome anger with calm, harm with good, the liar with truth.

teachings.text: There never was, there never will be, and there is not now anyone who is only blamed or only praised.
teachings.shortText: No one has ever been only blamed, or only praised.

teachings.text: As a smith removes the impurities from silver, the wise remove their own impurities, little by little, moment by moment.
teachings.shortText: As a smith purifies silver, the wise purify themselves, little by little.

teachings.text: There is no fire like desire, no grip like hatred, no net like delusion, no river like craving.
teachings.shortText: There is no fire like desire, and no river like craving.

teachings.text: The faults of others are easy to see; one's own are hard to see.
teachings.shortText: The faults of others are easy to see; one's own are hard to see.

teachings.text: You yourself must make the effort. The Buddhas only show the way.
teachings.shortText: You yourself must make the effort. The Buddhas only show the way.

teachings.text: “All conditioned things are impermanent.” When one sees this with wisdom, one grows weary of suffering. This is the path to purity.
teachings.shortText: All conditioned things are impermanent. Seeing this is the path to purity.

teachings.text: From meditation, wisdom arises; without meditation, wisdom fades. Knowing these two paths, live so that wisdom grows.
teachings.shortText: From meditation, wisdom arises. Without it, wisdom fades.

teachings.text: The gift of the teaching surpasses all gifts; the taste of the teaching surpasses all tastes; delight in the teaching surpasses all delights.
teachings.shortText: The gift of the teaching surpasses all other gifts.
